chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yahya ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, from Abdullah al-Anbary, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the man bury his son?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He cannot bury him in the soil.' I said, 'So can the son bury his father?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in burial rules between a father and a son in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights a nuanced distinction in Shia burial jurisprudence, where burying a son directly in the earth is often interpreted as a sign of humility or specific ritual status, contrasting with the permissibility of burying a father. Scholars note this reflects the hierarchical respect due to parents while acknowledging the natural order of generations, a practice rooted in the customs of the Ahl al-Bayt. The ruling underscores the importance of intention and ritual purity in interment, distinguishing it from general burial norms.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yahya Bin Amro, from Abdullah Bin Rashid, from Abdullah Al Anbary who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man bury his son?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He cannot bury him in the soil’. I said, ‘So can the son bury his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yahya ibn ‘Amr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Rashid from ‘Abd Allah al-‘Anbariy who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can a man bury his son?’ He replied, ‘He does not bury him in the soil.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘Can a son bury his father?’ He replied, ‘Yes, there is no offense in it.’”
